global_caption: The video consists of 10 shots and features a low-saturation pixel-art style fantasy indoor saxophone solo. The narrative structure follows a continuous exploration through a space connecting an office and a café. The visual tone is predominantly cool gray, accented with subtle warm amber hues along window edges and steam backlit by light. The camera movement begins with a reserved, gradual build-up, progressing toward a high-note climax before slowly receding. The The overall mood remains consistently subdued and immersive, with the performance featuring “低音三拍引子、穿廊切分短句、窗边长音展开、密集按键推进、高音扬升、尾音回旋收束”.
shot1: Shot 1 opens with a hard cut, wide eye-level shot establishing the night office. Foreground features low-resolution desks and dim monitor glow; midground shows the opening to the corridor; background faintly reveals warm cafe lighting. Composition uses office partitions and ceiling light lines to draw attention to the central dragon. Cool gray fluorescent lighting dominates, with slight screen reflections on desk edges. The dragon stands beside a chair, bends down to pick up the saxophone, with slight pixel jitter on wing membranes and tail tip.
shot2: Shot 2 follows with a hard cut, close-up overhead view of the dragon’s claw and saxophone keys. Lighting continues cool gray tone, with only fine highlights on key edges. Camera makes a small lateral pan, fully synchronizing key movements with each inhalation.
shot3: Shot 3 transitions via action-matched hard cut to medium-wide eye-level side-follow tracking. Camera moves along the corridor, following the dragon from office into the connecting passage to the cafe. Foreground sweeps past door frames and pixelated potted plants; background elevator indicator lights flash slowly, forming rhythmic reference. Cold corridor ceiling lights still dominate, but warm tones from the cafe begin to seep in. The dragon walks while stabilizing the instrument, tail swaying gently, shoulders rising and falling, initiating the first brief notes.
shot4: Shot 4 transitions via fade-in spatial shift to medium eye-level shot. Composition places the window-side position on the right, left side retains bar and seating layers. Window frame and tile perspective converge on the stationary dragon. Warm amber window light blends with cool interior lighting, creating unified low-saturation depth. Dragon stands by the window, raises the horn mouthpiece, and slowly plays the first complete phrase. Chest expands, throat relaxes, sustained tone flows steadily across the frame.
shot5: Shot 5 cuts hard to side close-up eye-level. Foreground includes curved horn body and blurred window light spots; focus locked on dragon’s cheek, neck side, and hand on keys. Shallow depth of field keeps facial pulsation and claw motion both sharp. Lighting continues warm edge outlining contours, cool interior suppressing background. Dragon enters denser phrases, cheeks and neck rhythmically pulsing, exhalation strength clearly increasing. Camera performs short dolly move, speed matching increasing phrase density.
shot6: Bar, open kitchen, coffee machine, and steam vents form geometric blocks below; dragon playing by the window occupies upper-right area. Spatial hierarchy is clear. Main lighting remains cool gray ambient, white steam from coffee machine creates soft backlight under warm accent light. Metal utensils in open kitchen vibrate subtly. Dragon’s long and short phrases spread throughout the space.
shot7: Shot 7 transitions via fade-in/fade-out to medium eye-level outside the second-floor glass classroom. Foreground shows pixelated light dots reflected on glass; background reveals lower cafe and window-side performer. Composition uses glass frame to divide inner and outer layers. Focus lies between swirling pixel light dots on glass and distant dragon silhouette. Lighting maintains cool-warm mix but overall low saturation. As Camera slowly pushes toward glass, each melodic rise increasing dot density.
shot8: Shot 8 cuts hard to low-angle medium-close shot. View from beneath the horn, saxophone bell and dragon’s raised jaw dominate frame. Background includes window signs and hanging lights, forming upward leading lines. Warm edge light outlines scales, cool environment darkens background. Dragon lifts head into high-note section, chest and back simultaneously engage, wing membrane slightly spreads, throat tenses then releases. High note peaks here. Camera performs rapid low-angle push-in, aligning highest note with maximum head elevation. Emotion shifts briefly from immersion to uplift.
shot9: Shot 9 cuts hard at climax to extreme close-up. Lens nearly touches key rods and hands. Foreground shows fast-moving blurred key shadows; focus locked on vibrating levers, claw tips, and tiny condensation droplets on horn surface. Background reduced to blurred fan blade light spots. Cool gray tone reclaims color palette, with minor warm reflections on metal edges. Camera applies minimal handheld-like front-back pulse, enhancing physicality of each press and quick inhale.
shot10: Shot 10 transitions via slow rack-focus followed by hard cut to wide eye-level view of entire cafe. Foreground includes tables, chairs, and bar edge; midground features dragon standing by window; background extends to corridor entrance and night office, completing spatial bookend. Overall lighting returns to unified cool gray and soft warm window blend. Pixel signboard on wall gently flickers with final note’s end, then fades out. Camera continuously pulls back, enclosing the entire performance within full space, precisely synchronizing last long note with signboard extinction.
